declarations.name: Causal.ChartIso.causallyConvexIn_image_iff
declarations.statement: ChartIso C D e → W ≤ chartSource e → V ⊆ W → (C.CausallyConvexIn V W ↔ D.CausallyConvexIn (e '' V) (chartImage e W))
declarations.standing: model-free core (1): 'a ChartIso transports causal convexity in W ≤ chartSource'. The relations of W are read through the chart; injectivity on the source gives the converse.

declarations.name: Causal.ChartIso.stronglyCausalOn_iff
declarations.statement: ChartIso C D e → W ≤ chartSource e → (C.StronglyCausalOn W ↔ D.StronglyCausalOn (chartImage e W))
declarations.standing: (1) 'a Causal.ChartIso carries StronglyCausalOn', both directions, for every open W in the source. Neighbourhoods move by OpenPartialHomeomorph.image_mem_nhds and continuousAt(_symm); convexity moves by the lemma above.

declarations.name: Causal.ChartIso.stronglyCausalOn_of_le, Causal.ChartIso.stronglyCausalOn_chartSource
declarations.statement: ChartIso C D e → W ≤ chartSource e → D.StronglyCausalOn (chartImage e W) → C.StronglyCausalOn W; ChartIso C D e → D.StronglyCausal → C.StronglyCausalOn (chartSource e)
declarations.standing: corollaries. The second goes through stronglyCausalOn_top and StronglyCausalOn.mono.

declarations.name: Causal.Causality.locallyStronglyCausal_of_chartIso
declarations.statement: (∀ p : M, ∃ (X : Type v) (_ : TopologicalSpace X) (D : Causality X) (e : OpenPartialHomeomorph M X), p ∈ e.source ∧ ChartIso C D e ∧ D.LocallyStronglyCausal) → C.LocallyStronglyCausal
declarations.standing: (1) 'a causality chart-isomorphic near each point to strongly causal ones is locally strongly causal', with a model for each point. ⚠ weakened: the models need only be locally strongly causal. W = e.source ∩ e⁻¹(W') for a strongly causal W' ∋ e p of the model.

declarations.name: Causal.Causality.locallyStronglyCausal_of_forall_chartIso, Causal.Causality.locallyStronglyCausal_of_forall_chartIso_of_stronglyCausal
declarations.statement: D.LocallyStronglyCausal → (∀ p, ∃ e, p ∈ e.source ∧ ChartIso C D e) → C.LocallyStronglyCausal; D.StronglyCausal → (same) → C.LocallyStronglyCausal
declarations.standing: the one-model forms; the second is what the flat instance uses.

declarations.name: Causal.IsCausalIso.stronglyCausalOn_iff, Causal.IsCausalIso.locallyStronglyCausal_iff
declarations.statement: IsCausalIso C D e → (C.StronglyCausalOn W ↔ D.StronglyCausalOn (e.opensCongr W)); IsCausalIso C D e → (C.LocallyStronglyCausal ↔ D.LocallyStronglyCausal)

declarations.name: Causal.Flat.locallyStronglyCausal_of_chartIso_chartAt
declarations.statement: ∀ {M} [TopologicalSpace M] [ChartedSpace (Minkowski d) M] {C : Causality M}, (∀ x, ChartIso C (minkowski d) (chartAt (Minkowski d) x)) → C.LocallyStronglyCausal

findings: The ladder's argued claim is true and now proved (programme/ladder.toml: the cylinder bullet of the locally_strongly_causal [[open]] section comment, :5660–5668 as read at 22:41 UTC, and the note of [[open]] locally_strongly_causal → is_causal, :5772–5775). The flat time cylinder, and the timelike circle at d = 0, are locally strongly causal. The proof is shorter than the note's and needs neither the covering map nor a small Minkowski ball. The chart at a point is a ChartIso onto minkowski d, minkowski d is strongly causal for every d (so d = 0 needs no separate timelike-line argument), and a ChartIso carries StronglyCausalOn. The chart's whole source is strongly causal as a spacetime.

Stronger than the target in three places. (a) The transport needs only locally strongly causal models, a model per point (Causality.locallyStronglyCausal_of_chartIso). (b) Every causality whose chart at each point is a ChartIso onto minkowski d is locally strongly causal (Flat.locallyStronglyCausal_of_chartIso_chartAt). That needs no HasGroupoid and no absolute minimality, so it holds in the no-gluing reading for the non-minimal causalities with the chart condition as well. (c) locally_strongly_causal is invariant under causal isomorphisms (IsCausalIso.locallyStronglyCausal_iff), which the node lacked.

Argued, not formalized: chart sources can be large. On ℤe₀\𝐌ⁿ the inverse of the projection on the slab {0 < t < 1} should be a chart of the maximal atlas, since its transitions are time translations. If so, the cylinder minus one slice, a dense open set, is strongly causal as a spacetime while the cylinder is not. The membership of that chart in the maximal atlas is not proved here.
No finding against ETT.tex: the target has no paper label.

kb_proposals: Strong causality through charts: Causal.ChartIso.stronglyCausalOn_iff (CausalScaffold.StronglyCausalTransport, ETT layer) says W ≤ chartSource e is strongly causal as a spacetime iff chartImage e W is. Causality.locallyStronglyCausal_of_chartIso: chart-isomorphic near each point to locally strongly causal models ⇒ LocallyStronglyCausal. For a model chart use …_of_forall_chartIso_of_stronglyCausal with the model's StronglyCausal. Every flat spacetime is locally strongly causal (Causal.Flat.flatCausality_locallyStronglyCausal), so the flat time cylinder is locally strongly causal and not strongly causal (T-loc-time-cylinder-lsc).

Pitfall: destructuring a long conjunction in term mode (`let ⟨h₀, …, h₁₀⟩ := thm; ⟨…⟩`, kb/0276's pattern) compiles to an auxiliary `match_1_1` whose kernel check took 6.2 s at timeCylinder 0 (trace.profiler: '[Kernel] typechecking declarations [….match_1_1]'). `by obtain ⟨…⟩ := thm; exact ⟨…⟩` took 1.2 s for the whole module. Prefer obtain when re-conjoining a separation (T-loc-time-cylinder-lsc).
